subject: nineTailedKitsune
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: nine-tailed kitsune fox with spirit flames.
Style: high-fantasy anime.

For the head itself, I'm thinking through its position as the neck's endpoint and planning to build the skull as a broad sphere with a tapered snout swept using local coordinate axes for forward, up, and right.

Rather than fight with left/right orientation ambiguity, I realize it's simpler and more robust to compute explicit world-space points for the head center and reference everything to the head bone directly, sidestepping the local-axis confusion entirely.

Still placing head geometry... now I need cheek ruffs — flattened spike blades sweeping out and back from the sides of the head, built with a small tuft helper function for consistent placement.

width direction, y the length direction. Now I'm placing the eyes using anime-style eye decals on the skull, picking a golden/amber kitsune iris color with red kumadori accent lines, and checking that the decal position falls within the skull's ellipsoid bounds using the point-in-ellipsoid distance formula.
